To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the efficiency of star formation in disk galaxies is correlated to the mass of the disk and that in elliptical galaxies it is high and not correlated with galaxy mass.

the efficiency of star formation in disk galaxies increases with the maximum rotation velocity, whereas in elliptical galaxies it is independent of the central velocity dispersion, and that the fraction of metals and gas expelled by outflows in elliptical galaxies increases with the mass of the galaxy.

the star formation efficiency is the main driver of galaxy formation in disks, and that in early-type galaxies, the star formation efficiency and gas outflows are the main drivers of galaxy evolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the evolution of galaxies in the local universe.
the study of star formation in the local universe.
the study of star formation in the Universe, with particular emphasis on the formation of the first galaxies and the formation of stars and galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
star formation in disk galaxies is driven by the amount of gas available to form stars, and the efficiency of star formation is a decreasing function of the maximum rotational speed.
the physics of star formation is not well understood.
star formation is more efficient in massive disks, whereas the star formation efficiency is independent of the mass of elliptical galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the observed properties of disk and elliptic galaxies can be understood by assuming that star formation is driven by a steep dependence of the star formation efficiency on the maximum rotation velocity in disk galaxies and a strong dependence on the galaxy mass in elliptical systems.
the star formation history of disk galaxies is mainly determined by the amount of gas available, whereas in elliptical galaxies the star formation is driven by internal processes.
star formation is a local process in disk galaxies, whereas in ellipticals the star formation efficiency is a constant, and outflows are important to explain the colors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a small number of parameters can describe star formation in galaxies.
the star formation efficiency and outflows can explain the main properties of disk and ellipticals galaxies.

a simple, physically-motivated, and phenomenological model of galaxy formation, based on a small number of physical parameters, can explain the observed correlations between galaxy properties and their star formation histories.
